questions.q: How did the guides and travellers climb up the steep wood to reach Cluny's Cage?
choices: By using the tree trunks like the rounds of a ladder
By following a hidden staircase cut into the rock
By pulling themselves up a rope let down from the top
By walking up a winding path along a mountain stream
questions.evidence: their trunks were like the rounds of a ladder, by which we mounted

questions.q: What served as the living centre-beam of the Cage's roof?
choices: A tree growing out from the hillside
An old ship's mast carried up the hill
A long slab of stone from the cliff face
Two crossed pine logs tied with rope
questions.evidence: A tree, which grew out from the hillside, was the living centre-beam of the roof

questions.q: Why was the fireplace built against a projection of the cliff?
choices: So the smoke, rising against rock of the same colour, would not be seen
So the heat stored in the rock would keep the Cage warm all through the winter
So the cooking could be done without any danger of fire to the walls
So water running down the cliff could be caught for the cooking

questions.q: How did Cluny stay safe for so long while others fled or were taken?
choices: He moved between hiding-places on his scouts' reports
He paid the soldiers to leave his part of the country alone
He disguised himself as a poor shepherd and lived in the open
He hid in one deep cave that no soldier ever found
questions.evidence: he moved from one to another as the soldiers drew near or moved away

questions.q: How did Cluny look and act when he greeted Alan and David?
choices: Plainly dressed in a nightcap, but with the manners of a king
Dressed in fine clothes and a sword, but rude and suspicious
Ragged and dirty, and too frightened to rise from his seat
Wearing a soldier's red coat, and laughing loudly and rudely at them
questions.evidence: For all that he had the manners of a king

questions.q: What toast did Cluny give when they all drank together?
choices: The Restoration
King George
The Laird of Shaws
Clan Macpherson
questions.evidence: here's a toast to ye: The Restoration!

questions.q: Cluny says, "My life is a bit driegh," and explains he sees little company and twirls his thumbs. What does "driegh" mean?
choices: Dull and tiresome
Dangerous and wild
Rich and comfortable
Short and happy
questions.evidence: I see little company, and sit and twirl my thumbs

questions.q: What kind of habits had Cluny developed in his long hiding?
choices: Precise habits, like an old maid, with his own seat no one else could use
Careless habits, leaving his things scattered all over the Cage floor
Brave habits, going out alone each night to spy on the soldiers
Lazy habits, sleeping most of the day and letting his gillies decide everything
questions.evidence: Cluny had grown to have all manner of precise habits, like those of an old maid

questions.q: Who shaved Cluny each morning and brought him the news of the country?
choices: A gillie who was a barber
His wife, who came by night
Alan Breck Stewart
A scout from the south
questions.evidence: one of them, who was a barber, came and shaved him

questions.q: What does it show that men of his clan paid money and laid aside revenge at Cluny's word?
choices: Even hunted and in hiding, he still ruled his clan as their chief
His clan was afraid that he would betray them to the red-coats
The courts of Scotland had ordered his clan to obey him
The men wanted his money and hoped to be paid well for all of their help
questions.evidence: he still exercised a patriarchal justice in his clan

questions.q: According to Cluny's stories, who had once stayed in the Cage before?
choices: Prince Charlie
King George
Colin Campbell
Alan's old father
questions.evidence: Cluny entertained us with stories of Prince Charlie's stay in the Cage

questions.q: Why did David refuse to play cards after the meal?
choices: His father had taught him gambling was wrong, and he had promised
He had no money of his own left and did not want to borrow
He did not know any of the games that Cluny wanted to play
He thought that Cluny was a cheat and would take every penny of his money
questions.evidence: it was a promise to my father

questions.q: What did Alan do right after Cluny called David's refusal Whiggish, canting talk?
choices: Spoke up for David as an honest gentleman and offered to play Cluny himself
Told David to stop being foolish and sit down to play at once
Laughed at David along with Cluny and poured another dram
Stood up and said that he and David would leave the Cage and go on their way at once
questions.evidence: I will put my hand in the fire for Mr. Balfour

questions.q: What happened to David during most of the time they stayed in the Cage?
choices: He lay sick in a kind of trance of fever
He went out each day with Cluny's scouts
He played cards with the gillies by the fire
He wrote letters to Mr. Campbell and Mr. Rankeillor
questions.evidence: I fell into a kind of trance

questions.q: On the second day, what did Alan ask David for while David lay feverish?
choices: A loan of his money
The silver button
His pistol and powder
A promise to stay
questions.evidence: He asked me for a loan of my money

questions.q: When David came back on the third day and saw papers but no gold on the table, all on Cluny's side, what did he begin to suspect?
choices: That Alan had lost all their money at cards
That Cluny had paid the scouts to keep them there
That the gold had been hidden from the soldiers
That Alan had won and put the gold in his purse
questions.evidence: I began to have a strong misgiving

questions.q: How did Alan behave when he admitted losing the money?
choices: He was ashamed and kept looking at the ground
He was angry and blamed Cluny for cheating
He laughed and said they would win it back
He was proud and said a gentleman never minds losing
questions.evidence: Alan said nothing, only looked on the ground

questions.q: Why did David find it painful to take the money back from Cluny?
choices: Taking back money fairly lost was hard on a man of pride
He feared Cluny would tell the soldiers where they were
He thought the gold was stolen from the king's soldiers
He believed that Alan would only gamble it all away again
questions.evidence: it must be hard upon a man of any pride

questions.q: What is the main thing that happens in this chapter?
choices: Alan gambles their money away in Cluny's hideout, and David must ask for it back
Cluny captures David and Alan and holds them as prisoners in the Cage until a ransom is paid
David nurses Alan through a fever while Cluny's men fight off the soldiers
David wins a great sum from Cluny at cards and buys passage to France
questions.evidence: I've lost it; there's the naked truth
